newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China bars Hong Kong pro-democracy politicians.
newsitem.headline: China bars Hong Kong pro-democracy politicians.

text.p: Chinese authorities barred two Hong Kong pro-democracy advocates from entering the country on Thursday and confiscated a travel document, one of them said.
Chinese officials at the Sha Tau Kok border post refused entry to Andrew To and Chan Kwok-leung of the Democratic Party after keeping them in a room for two hours, To told Reuters.
"They didn't explain. They said it was their superiors' instruction," To said, adding that they had confiscated his travel document.
The incident took place at a time of anxiety in Hong Kong about political freedom after China's recent crackdown on dissidents. Hong Kong will revert to China from Britain next year.

To and Chan, together with fellow advocates Chui Pak-tai and Wong Chung-ki, had planned to go to Beijing to petition a committee that is working on arrangements for Hong Kong's return to Chinese rule next July 1.

The petition urged Beijing to scrap a plan to appoint a provisional legislature in place of the elected Legislative Council, and demanded the territory's future leader be elected by the people instead of chosen by a China-controlled selection committee.
Chui and Wong were allowed into China. To said he could not explain why he and Chan were barred while the others were admitted.
Chinese officials were not available to comment.
To and Tsui are district councillors and Chan and Wong are urban councillors.
